rationale: Painterly-cluster committed hard: every material is 2-3 deliberate hand-placed value clusters with a shaped shadow edge, zero dithering, and one continuous plum-black #120b10 contour. The light is a single upper-left key consistent with a 2:1 dimetric down-camera, so top planes get their own dedicated value (A #b3ab7e on shoulder caps, forearm tops, fist knuckles, boot cuffs) rather than a gradient. The biggest confident brushstroke is the cast shadow the collar and jaw throw across the upper chest (rows 27-29) — a 10px-wide dark wedge that does the structural work of proving the head sits FORWARD of the shoulder plane, not level with it. Proportions are 3.3 heads: an 18px head over a 60px figure, shoulders 34px wide against a 24px head, fists 9-10px across, and a med-injector whose body plus magazine occupies 10x11px. Palette is 24 colours in a warm olive-drab / leather / rust family anchored on plum-black, with rust (#bc5b2c) at ~15% carrying medic identity via epaulettes, collar edge and belt buckle, and teal (#3fb5a2 / #d8fff0) held to a ~20px emission budget in the goggle glints and the injector charge window. What it sacrifices: no rendered fabric texture or wear-chipping — surfaces are frank flat clusters, so at 6x it reads as gouache blocks rather than rendered cloth. The pose is a static planted front stance with both arms down, which forfeits silhouette drama (no negative-space hole at the elbow) in exchange for an unambiguous front read. Symmetry is near-total apart from the weapon, so the asymmetric interest all sits low-right.
frontFacingCue: Four stacked cues, all in value not just colour. (1) A full-width goggle band at rows 9-11: bone rim #cdc4ad over cool glass #8fada6 with two hot #d8fff0 glints, sitting on a dark leather strap — the highest-contrast horizontal event in the sprite and unmistakably a pair of lenses aimed at the camera. (2) A lit forehead plane breaking through the hairline at rows 7-8 in the brightest skin #f2c194, with hair falling on BOTH cheeks (rows 12-15) so the bright face is framed left and right — you cannot read a framed face as a back of a head. (3) A vertical face structure below the goggles: lit nose column, a 4px dark mouth bar at row 15, and a lit chin at rows 16-19. (4) A hard silhouette step at row 16 where the 20px hair mass drops to a 14px bare jaw, which is the classic read for "head, seen from the front". For head/shoulder separation: chin at row 19, a 3-row bare neck in deep shadow #54302f, then a bone field collar (rows 22-26) that is the lightest band in the whole figure, then shoulders only start ramping at row 25 and don't reach full width until row 27 — leaving visible background sky on both sides of the neck. Nothing rises above the shoulder line; the weapon is at hip height and there is no pack.
smallCheck: Honest verdict: it survives, with one loss. I rendered a box-filtered 21x28 downscale onto the dark board and inspected it at 8x. What holds: the head reads as a head and reads as facing you — the dark hair mass, the pale goggle band, and the lit face below it stay as three distinct horizontal bands, and the head still visibly clears the shoulders because the bone collar survives as a bright pixel row. The rust epaulettes survive as two warm shoulder blobs framing the head. The chest emblem survives as a bright square, and the teal injector window survives as a single cyan dot that reads as "carrying tech". The two-legged stance and the light boot band both hold. What is lost: the cross stops being a cross and becomes a bright rectangle — at 28px tall the 8px patch is under 4px, so the arms of the cross fall below one pixel. The medic read at that size is carried by "bright emblem centred on the chest" plus the bone collar, not by cross geometry. Also lost: the mouth, the nose, and the thumb, and the weapon degrades from a legible pistol to a grey lump with a cyan dot. My recommendation if the 28px config is chosen: nothing here needs re-authoring, but the cross should be re-cut as a dedicated small-size variant rather than downscaled.
